In the 12-14 years race the Bels did very well to be placed 5th in the team race. Best performance was shown by Arnold Bent who only just 13 years old produced the best run of the day for the club in finishing 15th.
Of particular merit are those of Arnold Bent (5'1" High Jump at the age of 13),D.Thorogate(132'10" Discus),and John Barnard (10.9sec 100yards and 2nd in the All England Schools Championships).

We are sorry to hear of an injury to Arnold Bent who damaged his ankle whilst training at Battersea Park recently. Arnold,only 14½,shows great promise with a 19'0" long jump and a 5'1" high jump to his credit.On this particular occasion he cleared 20'0" for the first time in training.
In the Boys events winners were A.Bent (100y) and J.Lewis (880y). Generally then,a disappointing meeting especially for the handfull of spectators who did take the trouble to come.
The progress of that outstanding 15 year old high jumper ARNOLD BENT, still continues. Under the careful eye of coach Dave Ansell,Arnold has now reached 5'8" in his training sessions.
Youth jumper Arnold Bent has been bugged by injury lately but still regularly notches up wins for us, his best clearances being a 5'8" High Jump (Junior and Youth Records) and a Long Jump of 20'6½".
He finished off the evening with a 54.6 'quarter' behind Philip Gee's 53.5. The High Jump was a push over for Arnold Bent who won easily with 5'1", still having a further 7 or 8 inches in hand .

Arnold Bent took the Long Jump with 19'10" and a good 2nd place was gained by Gray in the Shot. Consistently in the 52.0 sec. range, Tony Brooks looks set to do well in the more important championships lined up in the next few weeks.
John Lewis was a worthy 3rd. and Robert Hamilton 4th. Arnold Bent was the only competitor in the High Jump. Perhaps it is his reputation that scares all the opposition away.

Senior Club Records were set by John Thresher (2m), Barry Townsend (Decathlon) Malcolm Robinson (3m), Geoff North (3m), John Bicourt (3000mSC) and equalled by Colin Clair (Jav). Youth Club Record was set by Arnold Bent (HJ) also equalling the Junior mark. For Belgrave Field Event Ranking List see page 42.
The Javelin and Triple Jump were cancelled due to the heavy rain but this did not deter Arnold Bent (Yth) from producing his best ever High Jump leap in competition - 5'9"!

Amongst the Youths Arnold Bent and Steve White stand supreme. With sprinter David Rees, John and Bob Hamilton over the 'half' and 'quarter' and new members Michael and Trevor Day and John Crockford over the longer distances, we have the makings of a first class Youth team.

Arnold Bent had no difficulty in winning the High Jump with 5'7", failing narrowly at 5'9" (the County record). Arnold regularly clears these heights and more in training but seems to be finding difficulty in following them up in competition.

Arnold Bent, the only Youth in the Senior High Jump, showed great form by clearing 5'8" and taking second place. Derek Wade was second in the Long Jump with 22'0" and has his sights on 24'0" this coming season with every chance of achieving it.

The fine array of 21 trophies on view were largley hogged by Nick Head (Javelin, Weight, Discus), Jim Vivian (100,220,440), Tony Brooks (Jun 220, Jun 440) and Arnold Bent (Sen and Jun high jumps), but performances were not quite up to expectations.

Bill Curtin ran his best race yet - 2:05.0 for the 880y - in his heat, a time that was not beaten even in the final, but here Bill was badly boxed in and could only get up to 5th with 2:09.4. Arnold Bent was 6th in the High Jump with 5'8 and Steve White was a member of the winning London Relay Team.

We have never had it so good in this event with Arnold Bent (Junior) already clearing 6'1½" this season Barry Townsend 5'10", Denzil Winsborrow 5'8" and Shola Ipaye 5'8" we could well have both A and B strings over 6 feet.

A fine run by John Dear in the steeplechase and a promising 440 by Jim Vivian on the last leg of the medly relay were also noteworthy, but the finest performance of the afternoon was undoubtedly the 6'-0" high jump of our junior, Arnold Bent.
Arnold Bent's 6'-1½" high jump at Crystal Palace rates him 15th in the U.K. 1968 best performance list and he is only a junior too!

Arnold Bent repeated his Sen/Jnr high jump double of last year and Bob Couillault clinched a useful triple/long jump double. Carl Lawton had a stylish win in the 2 miles walk after a fast start by Brian Ward that suggested an upset was due.

Just to show that we were not a one man outfit Arnold Bent turned on the heat with a Junior high jump win of 6'-1" and, to keep Steve company, finished runner-up in the long-jump just 7" behind his club mate.
At the London Schools Championships at Crystal Palace on June 15th ARNOLD BENT became the nation's No.1 high-jumper when he cleared the remarkable height of 6'-3".
After all, if Derek Boosey and Arnold Bent had been available our points score would very likely have been boosted to 36 or 37---by such margins are these trophies won or lost.

Dave Rees got us away to a fine start handing over with a lead to Mick Franks who increased this with great power and completed a great batton change with Arnold Bent who ran superbly to give John Hamilton a clear lead over the rest of the field.

Gerard's School Championships Mark Waight pulled off a treble by taking the Junior 100, 220 and 440 yards titles. Also at this school is John Hickey who is doing some fine hurdling, we hear; and, of course, top-ranker of them all, Arnold Bent (6'-3" HJ)
Next to come was Arnold Bent in the Senior Boys (under 20) high jump. This, for me, was the biggest disappointment of the day.

Congratulations to Arnold Bent, picked as 1st reserve in junior international match England v Germany at Crystal Palace on 7th September. Bill Curtin won a fine 1500 metre race against a classy field in order to gain selection for the "London v Vienna v Israel" Schools match.

Title holders Steve White (21.7) and Lee Sullivan (21'-9½") had no difficulty in holding on to their number one positions in the Senior ranks, but Arnold Bent relinquished his high jump title to rival Alexander who won on the count back---both clearing 5'-9¾".
